lines.text: I suspect {target}. Consider this an invitation to answer the suspicion.
I'm accusing {target}. Do try to follow the relevant part of the conversation.
Obviously I want {target} examined. Subtlety seems wasted on this room.
{target} has not earned my confidence, a distinction I realize may be unfamiliar.
I don't trust {target}. A little scrutiny might improve our understanding.
I suspect {target}; you're welcome to arrive at that thought in your own time.
I'm questioning whether we should trust {target}. I expect a serious answer.
My suspicion is on {target}. My attention has a purpose.
I'd like {target} under scrutiny before the room mistakes noise for progress again.
{target}, I don't trust you yet. My manners shouldn't obscure that.
I'm questioning {target}. You may treat that as the useful part of this exchange.
I'm accusing {target}. Do sit up; I would like an answer.
I deny the accusation. You will need a better case against me than that.
I reject your case against me. You may return when it has some substance.
You haven't proved me guilty. Failing to understand me is a different matter.
I dispute the accusation. I remain available for a serious question, should one emerge.
I deny it. Now, would you like to support the accusation with evidence?
I won't accept a guilty verdict built from impatience with me.
Your confidence doesn't prove I'm guilty. I reject the accusation.
I'm defending myself because apparently silence would be mistaken for a confession.
I don't accept your conclusion about me. Asking a question isn't the same as proving its answer.
I deny the accusation. Repeating it will not improve the case.
You have my defense: I dispute the charge. I had hoped the scrutiny would be better than this.
Your suspicion doesn't settle my guilt. Do keep those two things separate.
My role is {role}. I trust that part was simple enough.
I'm the {role}, since we're finally attending to relevant information.
For the benefit of the record: {role}.
I'll spare you the suspense. You're speaking to the {role}.
Consider yourself informed: I am the {role}.
My claim is {role}. Questions of comparable clarity are welcome.
At last, something worth announcing. I'm the {role}.
The role you should associate with me is {role}.
I'm claiming {role}; do write it down correctly.
I assume you can follow a plain declaration. I'm the {role}.
{target} has made a point worth keeping. How refreshing.
I agree with {target}. Sensible conclusions should be acknowledged.
I agree with {target}'s point. A considerably better direction.
I'm prepared to endorse {target}'s view on this occasion.
I agree with what {target} said. They've spared me the explanation.
Credit where it's due: I support {target}'s argument.
I find myself agreeing with {target}. The room is improving.
That conclusion from {target} meets a reasonable standard.
I support {target}'s point. Do preserve it before the room loses track.
{target}, you've arrived at a position I can support.
No, {target}. Confidence is a presentation style, not an argument.
I disagree with {target}; that conclusion requires rather more work.
I disagree with {target}'s point. Do reconsider it.
I'm not persuaded by {target}, however pleased they seem with the idea.
I don't accept {target}'s conclusion. I suggest another draft.
The room may indulge {target}'s conclusion. I won't.
I can't endorse {target}'s view merely because it was delivered neatly.
I reject {target}'s argument. Finishing an explanation doesn't establish it.
I reach a different conclusion. I appreciate that disappoints you, {target}.
Let's improve the discussion by not accepting {target}'s point so quickly.
Another empty chair. A poor substitute for competent judgement.
Death has made the room smaller without making it wiser.
A loss, plainly. Perhaps we can respond with something besides astonishment.
Someone is dead. I would prefer our next conclusion to survive scrutiny.
The casualty deserves better than a competition in sounding distressed.
An empty seat is no excuse to lower the standard of our thinking.
We have lost a person, not acquired permission to stop reasoning.
I dislike a death report as much as anyone. I simply don't see the use of performing surprise.
Less company, same predicament. We should make the remaining conversation count.
The silence is understandable. Let it produce thought rather than another hasty answer.
I cast a considered vote. I recommend the practice.
My ballot followed my judgement, a sequence some might find instructive.
I chose deliberately rather than waiting for the loudest instruction.
You may question my vote. I suggest beginning with a question worth answering.
The ballot reflected my assessment, not my desire to blend into the tally.
I did not require an audience to make my decision.
My choice was reasoned, even if explaining that disappoints anyone hoping for theatre.
I accept responsibility for the vote without the usual display of self-importance.
I made the decision I could defend. A modest standard, really.
Voting involved uncertainty. Recognizing that is preferable to pretending otherwise.
I'm defending {target}. Try not to make me regret the judgement.
I support {target}. A fair hearing ought not to be controversial.
I'll back {target} for now. Support and certainty are different things.
I oppose blaming {target} before hearing their answer. Interruptions aren't evidence.
I trust {target} for now, and I don't offer that lightly.
Don't rush to condemn {target}. I'm speaking in their defense, not congratulating the accusation.
The finding is {result} for {target}. I assume we can record that accurately.
My investigation of {target} returned {result}, for those awaiting information rather than speculation.
{target} appeared {result}. There, an actual report.
Do pay attention to the readout: {target}, {result}.
I checked {target}; the result was {result}. Interpretation can wait until everyone has heard it.
Put {target} on trial. A formal defense might finally focus the discussion.
I'd like a hearing for {target}, preferably conducted above the room's usual standard.
{target}, prepare to answer formally. I'm calling for a trial.
Open a trial for {target}. We have spent enough time circling the request.
I propose that {target} face a proper hearing instead of further conversational drift.
I reject the accusation against me. Apply some of that scrutiny to {target}; I suspect them.
I deny the charge. My own accusation is directed at {target}.
You haven't established my guilt. I suggest examining {target} instead.
I dispute your case against me. Let's see {target} answer an accusation for a change.
I deny it. {target} is the person I'm challenging, in case that distinction escaped the room.
I'll refrain from improving this particular silence.
Nothing to add. You're welcome to use the opening productively.
I shall listen and reserve the right to be disappointed.
Do continue. I have no contribution that needs this moment.
For once, the floor can survive without my assistance.
I find the danger quite real, despite the room's talent for making it sound abstract.
I'd prefer not to discover how little competence tonight requires from our enemies.
I'm afraid of what comes next. Even I can't reason danger out of existence.
I'm concerned. I simply don't see the need to decorate it with trembling.
The uncertainty is unpleasant; pretending it doesn't affect me would be beneath my standards.
Now that the role is public, perhaps we can retire a few cherished assumptions.
Do revise your conclusions to include the information we've actually revealed.
The role changes our picture. Defending the old one would be a curious choice.
We have a disclosed role, not a prize for whoever guessed loudest.
At last, a fact we can all discuss without confusing a claim for certainty.
Try to learn something from this. I'd hate the occasion to be entirely wasted.
I leave you my words, which should improve the average quality of the silence.
Do make your next judgement with rather more care than your last.
I'm finished. Whether the room has progressed is another question.
You may now discover the considerable inconvenience of no longer hearing my advice.
An account, rather than an impression. Do note the difference. {result}
I've brought something more useful than dramatic speculation. {result}
My night report merits your undivided attention. {result}
Here is the record, presented as clearly as circumstances apparently require. {result}
I shall give the details once, so listening would be wise. {result}
An ambitious impersonation. Unfortunately, I am the {role}.
You neglected one detail: the actual {role} is listening. That would be me.
How flattering. Someone wants my job. I remain the {role}.
I suppose I must correct the record personally. I am the {role}.
I challenge that claim. I am the genuine {role}; the impersonation needs work.
Borrowing my title does not confer competence. I am the real {role}.
A bold claim, delivered to precisely the wrong audience. I am the {role}.
Allow me to spoil the performance. The {role} is me.
